definition: Counter wills, also called mutual or reciprocal wills, are separate wills between two people that have identical or similar provisions leaving each person’s property to the other or to a third person. The agreement in a compact for mutual wills is that each person will dispose of his or her property in a certain way. The provision of each person leaving the other person their property is the consideration for the other. Counter wills are usually made between a married couple, and it is rare for them to execute a single counter will. It is also rare for counter wills to be made between more than two people.
